# What Mailchimp API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, written twice,
# which is the thirty-two characters of the body and which no real credential
# is. Behind the body stands the separator and the number of the data center the
# account is held in; that number is the data center's rather than the
# credential's, so it carries no run and is written as 19 wherever the number is
# not what a case is about.
#
# The cases about what the pattern leaves alone are built from the same run: in
# uppercase where the case is about the case, carried on through the alphabet
# where the value is longer than sixteen characters, and with more characters
# written after it where the case is about a run too long to be a body. The one
# case carrying no run is the region written after a word, which is a line with
# no body in it at all.

patterns: mailchimp-api-key

# The one shape Mailchimp issues for the Marketing API. A key reaches the whole
# of an account through that API — its audiences, the subscriber data behind
# them and the campaigns sent to them — with no scope on it to narrow what it
# can do, so there is a single kind of string here rather than a table of them.
# The cases below are that shape in the places a key is written.

case:     a key on its own
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19
out:      «mailchimp-api-key»

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19
out:      MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=«mailchimp-api-key»

case:     a key as the password of the basic authorization every call to the API carries
in:       curl --user "anystring:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19" https://us19.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/ping
out:      curl --user "anystring:«mailchimp-api-key»" https://us19.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/ping

case:     a key in the configuration of the client library Mailchimp publishes
in:       mailchimp.setConfig({apiKey: "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19", server: "us19"})
out:      mailchimp.setConfig({apiKey: "«mailchimp-api-key»", server: "us19"})

case:     a key in json
in:       {"apiKey":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19","server":"us19"}
out:      {"apiKey":"«mailchimp-api-key»","server":"us19"}

case:     a key in a log line
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info key=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info key=«mailchimp-api-key»

# The number behind the separator is read to the end of its digits with a floor
# of one, so the data center Mailchimp's own documentation names is located as
# readily as a two-digit one, and a number longer than any it has built is
# redacted whole rather than to its first two digits.

case:     a key whose data center number is one digit
in:       MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us6
out:      MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=«mailchimp-api-key»

case:     a key whose data center number is longer than any Mailchimp has numbered
in:       MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us123
out:      MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=«mailchimp-api-key»

# The body is held to being the whole of the run it stands in, which is what
# keeps a digest with a region written behind it out of this pattern. Thirty-two
# hexadecimal characters are an MD5 exactly, so the separator and a number are
# the whole of what tells a key from one; a longer digest is a run too long to
# be a body and is left where it stands, at either end of the run.

case:     an md5 with no separator behind it
in:       checksum=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      checksum=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha-1 in front of the separator
in:       artifact=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567-us19
out:      artifact=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567-us19

case:     a hexadecimal character written against the body
in:       MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=a0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19
out:      MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=a0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us19

# The separator and the number are read as they are written. The body's alphabet
# is lowercase hexadecimal alone, which is what the one rule reading a key that
# stands on its own reads it in.

case:     the separator with no number behind it
in:       MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us
out:      MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-us

case:     a region written after a word, with no body in front of it
in:       bucket=logs-us19
out:      bucket=logs-us19

case:     an uppercase body
in:       MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF-us19
out:      MAILCHIMP_API_KEY=0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF-us19

# The other Mailchimp credential this pattern's name covers and its grammar
# reaches nowhere: the Transactional API key, which is twenty-two characters
# with nothing in them to be recognised by.

case:     a transactional api key
in:       MANDRILL_API_KEY=0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      MANDRILL_API_KEY=0123456789abcdefghijkl
